item.description:
**Join us at Isis Oasis Sanctuary in Geyserville, California for a special evening of exploring the fascinating and allegedly haunted grounds of Isis Oasis Sanctuary. You'll hear some of the amazing history of this place and visit locations where residents and guests alike have reported unusual activity, plus a rare visit to our little-known Egyptian Tomb Room. Author deTraci Regula guides you on this tour which lasts approximately one hour. Bring a flashlight and be prepared to walk over some uneven ground and go up and down stairs. (Alternative accessible tour available on request.)**

item.title: Magdalena Open House: Walk Through a New Home You Can Lease and Buy — Thu Oct 29, 6:00 PM — Magdalena Home
item.description:
Come walk through a Magdalena home in Santa Rosa and see what life in a new factory-built home feels like: high ceilings, big windows, a full kitchen, a full bathroom with a modern shower, a washer/dryer and a sleeping loft.
Magdalena homes sit on wheels, so they can be towed to a backyard, family land or your own lot. Lease one for $980 a month plus site fee, live in it first, and buy it later at a locked price of $68,000 if it's right for you.
The open house is for reservation holders. Reserve a spot for $100, refundable anytime, at magdalena.one and we'll send you the address.
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat

item.title: Flynn Creek Circus Presents ‘The Cricket & the Wren’ — Fri Oct 30, 7:00 PM — Grange Hall Sebastopol
item.description: Flynn Creek Circus Presents ‘The Cricket & the Wren’: a highly original, all-human circus that enchants through breathtaking acrobatics and athletically stunning skill. Sponsored by the good folks at Sebastopol Grange. Sebastopol, CA— Oct 29 – Nov 1– This 2026 season, Flynn Creek Circus invites audiences to ‘The Cricket & the Wren’ — memorable family fun and Artful athleticism under the circus big top. A merchant’s daughter sets out to find the castle where the horizon meets the sea. In order to break the spell of the Frog Prince, she must brave a harrowing journey filled with wonder. Along the adventure, she encounters Jack and the Beanstalk’s sassy cow, an out of pocket Pirate and the secret sacrifice of the cricket and the wren. Featuring aerialists, jugglers, knife throwers, and laugh out loud comedy, this circus blends classic storybook archetypes with imaginative new heroes. The Cricket and the Wren will surprise, dazzle and delight all ages. In addition to the family friendly sh

item.title: Mary Collins School at Cherry Valley Presents Beetlejuice JR — Fri Oct 30, 7:00 PM — Mary Collins School at Cherry Vallet
item.description:
Something strange and unusual is coming to Mary Collins at Cherry Valley School! The school's Theater Arts Program (TAP) presents *Beetlejuice JR.*, running October 30–November 8, 2026, featuring two casts of talented young performers and a student technical crew bringing the beloved Broadway musical to life.
Under the leadership of Darby Ciampi, Lindsey Nettleton, and an experienced creative team, TAP delivers an ambitious theatrical experience that goes far beyond the stage. Students are involved in every aspect of production, from acting, singing, and choreography to lighting, sound, set construction, costumes, and props. With professional mentorship, students gain hands-on experience in the full theatrical process, developing creativity, confidence, and collaboration along the way.
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat

item.title: Mary Collins School at Cherry Valley Presents Beetlejuice JR — Sun Nov 1, 1:00 PM — Mary Collins School at Cherry Vallet
item.description:
Something strange and unusual is coming to Mary Collins at Cherry Valley School! The school's Theater Arts Program (TAP) presents *Beetlejuice JR.*, running October 30–November 8, 2026, featuring two casts of talented young performers and a student technical crew bringing the beloved Broadway musical to life.
Under the leadership of Darby Ciampi, Lindsey Nettleton, and an experienced creative team, TAP delivers an ambitious theatrical experience that goes far beyond the stage. Students are involved in every aspect of production, from acting, singing, and choreography to lighting, sound, set construction, costumes, and props. With professional mentorship, students gain hands-on experience in the full theatrical process, developing creativity, confidence, and collaboration along the way.
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat

item.description:
Dia de los Muertos \(Day of the Dead\) is a Latin American tradition, where we can all meet and remember our ancestors. Come experience the traditions of, art, music, Catrinas, and beautiful ofrendas as we gather in love and remembrance. Bring a photograph of a loved one who has passed and place it on our Community Altar/Ofrenda. Together, let’s create a place where memories, cultures, and hearts come together.
If you knew Calvin Ellington come, share your memories with Mario. If you never had the chance to meet Calvin, join us in celebrating love and the lasting mark our loved ones leave on our lives.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: DOMESTICATED by Patrick Atkinson - an original play reading — Sun Nov 1, 3:00 PM — Bay Area Stage Theatre
item.description:
Join us for a staged reading of DOMESTICATED, an original play by Patrick Atkinson, presented by Bay Area Stage Productions. Experience a new work in an intimate setting where story, language, and performance take center stage.
Domesticated tells the story of four pets living in a remote house in the country. Suddenly alone with no one to take care of them, they must find a way to survive. Along the way, they remember their lives with each other. It is a story of the joys and sorrows of living together, of how we remember and honor the friends we lose, and of the will to go on.
Cast: Maya Rath as Annie, Jessica Schild as Tina, Isaac Arriaga as Bob, Ginger Burnett as Suzette, Bill Chessman as Dave, Suzan Lorraine as Chloe, Amanda Beaton as Ensemble
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Cool Petaluma's 5th Annual Shindig: the Launch Party for Cool Future — Thu Nov 5, 5:00 PM — Hall of the Above
item.description:
Join Cool Petaluma for our 5th annual Shindig, a community mixer and fundraiser at the beautiful Hall of the Above!
This year, we’re celebrating something big: the launch of our new nonprofit, Cool Future. With your support, Cool Future will bring Cool Petaluma’s neighbor-to-neighbor climate resilience program, Cool Teams, to 4 more Northern CA cities in 2027. This grassroots movement started right here in Petaluma. Our ongoing neighborhood connection work in town⏤and our chance to share what we’ve learned⏤are made possible entirely by community members like you.
Enjoy tasty bites, local libations, and a stellar silent auction while you meet like-minded neighbors and catch up with old friends. Tickets start at $50. Event sponsorships are also available.
Every ticket sold helps keep this community-funded program growing!
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat
